Right, where do I begin?

Hacknet is a game with a lot of potential. I enjoyed it thoroughly, found the story to be very engaging, and the "think fast" moments were executed well enough for some noticeable pressure to kick in. The music and visuals work *really* well together to deliver a captivating experience.

However, Hacknet is not quite at a stage where I'd call it a full release. Right now, it looks more like a competent early access preview. The game is riddled with game-breaking bugs (What's that? You're a completionist and decided to do all quests for one faction before moving on to the next? I'm afraid you just got the storyline out of sync and will find yourself stuck shortly!) and a bit too short to make a strong case for the price tag. The severity of the bugs is somewhat mitigated by the simplicity of the save file format, so if you end up screwing yourself over, you can cheat your way around it.

All in all, Hacknet is a less advanced but still oh-so-enjoyable Uplink. If you already know Uplink and are looking for more of the same, you'll enjoy Hacknet despite its flaws. Since the game is still being actively patched by the dev, it will hopefully become even better over time.

So I've played the game a couple times through now, and I have some thoughts on it (and some pretty fun experiences).

The game is very fairly priced, and has a good portion of content with a good selection of paths you can take, though they all end up the same place, which possibly could be a turn-off. I've seen a couple bugs here and there, but it wasn't very difficult to deal with, or never long enough in where I dreaded to restart.

The story is really cool, albeit kind of easy to predict. It's very immersing though, and really gets going at a rapid pace. I enjoy it time and time again, and take my time to do the missions properly, although I know most of them and know which ones are "skippable".

Now, mechanics wise.. It gets kind of weird. It's very easy to get into, and you can pick it up and play the game to a finish "fairly" easily, but that's where it gets interesting. There's lots of small mechanics and tweaks you can make to the gameplay (renaming all but PortHack, having a trap shell set on yourself at all times, ect.), which ends out in you being able to dive deeper into it than just doing the base game. And if you enjoy collecting the different skins, then you have a lot of work to do (Looking at you, CCC hacksquad).

Now, onto the DLC.

The DLC brings a lot of things to the table. Instead of the mailbox, you're now in a chatroom with three other hackers. This leaves a door slightly open to get some really decent hints if you're stuck, and the general descriptions of the missions make it a lot easier to understand what you're doing when playing through the content for the first time. It also brings new mechanics, in that the ports will now be changing ever so often, without warning (though that's not much of a challenge, as long as you look at the port #'s before pressing enter, you're good). Now I do have a single warning though, if you haven't played through the DLC before.

[b] Make sure to check if the CMD prompts are actual Windows prompts or in-game prompts.[b] I got a scare when I had just worked my way through the prompt, only for my pc to reboot when i put in 'shutdown /r'. Just close the game, that's more than enough.

Overall, 9/10. Would've loved for some more content, and some bigger challenges. I was hoping the DLC would go the extra mile above the base game, but it sadly didn't. I can definitely recommend the game if you're looking for something different and something to puzzle yourself with. It requires a fairly keen eye.

Late review, but still... Hacknet is one of my favorite games and it was a really engaging experience. I often lost myself for hours in the game 'hacking' different servers/computers and I really recommend it to anyone who likes to puzzle a lot, while using unix. 

PRO's:
- Easy to learn, easy to master, but it doesn't make the game boring. On the contrary, it makes the game even more enjoyable, because (after mastering 'the controlls') you get the feeling of being a skilled 'hacker'.
- Probably the closest a game could get to real world hacking. Uplink was great too, but outdated and not as fun as Hacknet. Also great that you can use the 'GUI' to select hosts or use the command line to connect and perform functions.
- Great Soundtrack, really fits the 'hacking' experience and makes your heart beat a little bit faster during the most intense scenes. I downloaded the soundtrack after beating the game, because of the thrill you get from it.
- Great DLC (Hacknet Labrynths). I really liked the way that the Devs enabled players to make their own storylines, factions, puzzles, eastereggs, etc. while keeping the Hacknet game mechanics. I tried to make my own 'Extension', but after all it was harder than I thought. 
- Fun easter eggs. Took some time to get the last achievements, but it was totally worth it.

CON's:
- Storyline is too short and can be completed in a short time period. I almost felt sad when I completed the game (as there was DLC at the time, which meant that there was no new content to play).
- There are no consequnces to your actions. This means that you won't be attacked by enemies (in game of course) if you hack the wrong pc/server. Of course, there are some moments when a countdown is presented and you need to finish a task in a small amount of time, but besides that it gives you the feeling that nobody cares if they are hacked. Also, why should you ever clear logs and footprints when nobody will ever try to get you back using them?

Overall, definitely worth the money and it's a great game to get the 'hacking' vibe. Implementation of Extensions by the Devs makes the amount of content for this game even bigger, which means more storylines and time spent hacking with a cheeto dust covered keyboard.

Rating: 8/10

Rating: 11/10 would clear my OS files instead of my logs again.

Hacknet is a beautiful mix of ease of use and realism that really makes you feel like Neo from the matrix.

The progression in the game is fantasic starting you off preforming very simple tasks and slolwly introducing you to new game mechanics along the way.

I bought Uplink long time ago. That game sadly doesn't age well as the UI is way too small and I can't press on certain button. I wanted play a good hacking simulation game.

I got Hacknet for free, but truth to be told, I should've bought this game if I knew about it. Amazing UI, gameplay, story, works great on modern PC, and not to mention the soundtrack is super amazing and cues in on the right moment. I'm planning to get the DLC later just to play more of this.

The terminal mode is very similar to Unix systems like Linux. I've used a lot of different Linux distros in the past and used terminal extensively, and I have to say, this is an amazing level of detail coming from an indie game. It's very close to the Unix experience and I found myself naturally using it a lot.

Every systems here have reference to the real world hacking (whereas other hacking games are purely fictional), its just that it is simplified to the point where you can just type a few letters to run the program (like a script kiddie). You can hack almost every systems in the game. Almost everything is also self-consistent too, even the HTML source can be edited.

I wanted to praise more about what this game did right, but I don't want to spoil anything, so I'll say just say that this game, gives you an environment where you feel like you are a true hacker, and you are surrounded by 4chan-style hacking community. And once you managed to hack the hardest thing ever, it gives you great satisfaction about it.

Hacknet also blends command line with puzzle very well, feels very similar to real world hacking.

My only complain was that it was too short and I wished that there is more functionality in the command line and your OS to create new folders etc, but I guess it was ok for a game that's just about simulating hacking and not simulating everything.

Also, I've got 100% achievement on this game. I rarely do achievement for any games, but this game is worth doing the achievements as you learn more about this game.

Overall, this is the best script kiddie simulator that I've played thus far and you should definitely buy this game, 9/10.

This is the 3rd review I'm writing for this game, and honestly, when talking about this game, I am both bored and felt that it ended too soon.  The game is short, mind you.  It takes about 5 to 6 hours to complete.  Most of this time is spent fannying about, doing the games' equivilent of 'go there, kill 10 of these things', as the game frequently breaks you away from the main story/context to have you perform side missions, that usually boil down to 'hack x, delete y.'

Why am I recommending this game, saying it ended too soon?  I say this because the last two missions are two of the most cleverly crafted puzzles I've ever seen.  'Project Junebug' and 'Bit Foundation' are stellar works of glory.  I'll focus on Project Junebug, as the Bit Foundation is the final story mission (the story ends spectacularly, by the way).   Obvious spoiler alert for ahead.

The game's side missions usually work as a sort of key insert thing.   Hack 4 ports, using 4 specific commands you get earlier in the game, Port Hack, boom, in, done.  No challenge, besides when there's a tracer, but simply disconnect and reconnect, and you're good as gravy.

Project Junebug was shaping up to be another one of those things.  As I hacked the medical terminal, I thought it was clever, having to use intuition to find the IP for a heart monitor, to kill a guy.  Connecting to said IP, I found that it required access to Port 104, where up until that point I only found stuff for ports 22, 25, 28, 1433, and 88.  Not wishing to go further, it required me to hack several computers slightly hinted at, and it was brilliant, as it forced me to use inginuity and my brain to track it down.

Note to Developers:  If you made the game more like THAT, other than the slog through Entropy and CSEC, then you'd have my full support.  Say utilize the 'find and replace' skill more, or maybe give us some way to hack to second computer by using the first.  Just suggestions.

Hacknet is a puzzling mystery game where you take on the role of a hacker who must contribute to the computing world of hackers by breaking into systems with the use of special programs, navigate and modify files and data in such systems, and complete tasks for other people on the behalf of your faction. The game features the usage of actual terminal commands and coding in order to navigate the complex game, forcing the player to learn and adapt to the usage of this code quickly in order to press forward in game. The ultimate goal of the player is to discover the fate of a mysterious, experienced hacker that goes by the name of 'Bit', who helps out the player at the beginning on the game, allowing them to get up on their feet and stand a fighting chance against the brutal world of code.

The game is a decent length. For a slow gamer who wishes to experience and explore, this game usually takes ~15 hours to complete. Some quick cookies may find that they can complete the main story in as little as 5 hours, however.

Whether I recommend this to every player or not is quite trivial. An almost definite prerequisite for playing this game is the excellent ability to problem solve, and the capability to explore. This game isn't for every player out there, as there is certainly the possibility of frustration and boredom when the player cannot figure out what direction they should take or how to correctly solve one of the many challenging puzzles the game has to offer. For those that love to code and adore solving complex, challenging problems, this game is definitely a buy. If you see the game on sale grab it real quick!

I myself had a pleasant experience with this game, and definitely enjoyed the atmosphere and challenge the game has to offer. Reading the IRC logs in the various computer systems and getting a response when I cussed at an aggressive hacker was by far my favourite parts of this game.

- Googarai

review_text_raw:
[h1]Hacknet[/h1]

Hacknet is a game about hacking as the title might suggest.
I must admit that I have never played anything like this before.

The story was quite interesting and you progress by doing missions that consists of different tasks related to hacking.
You will change information in registries, search for specific information etc. To make this into interesting gameplay you use simple programming to achieve these things when performing hacks. 

As you progress you get access to new "hacking tools" and it becomes less casual. You will sometimes work against a timer while you hack and try to achieve the task at hand. I recommend watching a trailer or in game footage to get a better grasp of what I am talking about, how the hacking progress works.

Sometimes the game can be tricky and you might feel a bit lost. This happened to me on several occasions. 
Luckily there are some guides and helpful pages out there to help you out (Steam forums Reddit etc.).
It is also one of the most satisfying parts of the game; that you are in the dark and never really know how it all will end. 

The soundtrack is really nice. Electronic music while hacking and feeling the pressure of the time running out; it feels [b]intense[/b]!

[h1]To Conclude[/h1]
[list]
[*] Unique interesting game.
[*] Exciting story.
[*] Fantastic electronic music.
[*] Smart interaction of programming.
[*] Great start to learn some programming.
[*] Feels rewarding as you learn some new things and become more independent throughout the game.
[*] - To dumbed down for real hacker enthusiasts.

I got this game from humble bundle for free.
I always recommend going for the sales. 
9,99€ is a bit steep in my opinion for the content, would recommend pricing at 4,99€.
Of course there is Steam Workshops or you can buy the dlc for more content.
Nevertheless I highly recommend getting [b]Hacknet![/b]

review_text_raw:
Hacknet is, by far, the most enthralling and immersive hacking experience I've played to date. Adding the Labirynths expansion, the game excels at managing your stress levels: there are times of low intensity, times of high intensity, and times of crisis-level intensity. There are also times of "dead"-intensity; that is to say, lest you remember some of the basic mechanics of the game, it's possible at a few points to feel like whatever situation you're experiencing is not salvagable. With the emotional rollercoast also comes incredible use of comedic relief, a little extra sanding to take the edge off. 

Some of the best and brightest moments of Hacknet (and it's expansion) are when you'll find yourself laughing at an IRC log or stray text file's contents; some of them are when you'll find yourself scrambling to disconnect from a server before a trace locks in on your system; some of them are just... breathtaking, almost moving moments that could maybe bring you to tears, and yet further more are moments where your morality comes into play. 

I've only played through the game (and it's expansion) once; I understand that, while limited, there are various other paths and routes that the player may choose to take instead. I'm definitely going to play through the game several more times to find some more secrets and goodies. I'm also interested in the upcoming Hacknet Extensions update, which will bring modding tools and workshop functionality to the table, adding even more content. I'm excited as I'll get out.

I will say, however, if you're not particularly technically inclined, it might be a bit difficult to get going, actually. Don't panic though: most of the game's mechanics have reference material readily available in game, so if you ever forget syntax or a naming convention, it's easy to find the solution.

If you're interested in science-fiction action/mystery thrillers, then this is a game for you.

A neat little game. Too short in my opinion and the contracts aside from the main story felt a little too repetitve and bland but I enjoyed them.

What really drew me in was when I was first hacked, the panic that set in had my heart beating as i tried to figure out what was going. That and the final mission with Roller Mobster by Carpenter Brut playing? Hell yeah. I'm glad I can replay that whenever I want.

Overall this is a great game, really gets you thinking as you try and uncover the secret behind things. Just wish it was a bit longer and with more variety. I've yet to check out the expansion but I will once I get back to.

And again, Roller Mobster was a great song choice.

review_text_raw:
Hacknet was an experience like no other. Its unique gameplay, tense moments and solid storyline got me hooked the moment I got that first message from Bit.

As an introduction to hacking, it does its job, but nothing more. I wouldn't expect anyone to be able to hack the Pentagon after playing this game. However, that does not detract one bit from the overall experience. It has a solid difficulty curve, so even the most computer-illiterate people will not have too much trouble. It is intuitive, and most importantly it is fun. Base game Hacknet provides an amazing 8 hour experience that everyone should check out. Not to mention the soundtrack, which is phenomenal.

With the Labyrinths DLC, Hacknet gets even more content in the form of a new storyline, new programs, new music and new puzzles. There is not much else to say then, the quality is the same, arguably better in the DLC, and I would recommend purchasing the DLC along with the base game.

Finally, there is a reason why I have so many hours in this game. Despite how amazing it is, Hacknet's story is somewhat short being 8 hours long, plus the DLC taking it to around 12 hours. I have played through the entire game plus DLC multiple times, but those never would have taken me to 100+ hours of playtime. No, I'm talking about mod support for the game, Hacknet Extensions. Extensions allows people to create their own storylines, puzzles, campaigns, etc. for other people to play. There are already many extensions to play, and as an active extensions developer myself, I can definitely say they add to the replayability of the game.

A reasonably niche game that I would recommend to anyone who wants to try something different.

review_text_raw:
This game is great. There are a few lookalikes in the store and some of them are pretty good but Hacknet is the best so far. Do yourself a favor and pick up the Labyrinths DLC as it's about the same length as the main game and introduces new mechanics on top. The overall narrative in the DLC is also a little more interesting than in the main game.

The actual hacking of systems becomes mechanical and sort of tedious after a while, and the net map gets really hard to navigate, but the former is not a big enough issue to detract from the fun of exploration / exploitation and the latter can be partially solved with some (in-game) software you'll find in your adventures.

Extra points for a perfect soundtrack!
